title: Page Layout with Template Areas
description: Create a full page layout (header, sidebar, main, footer) using grid template areas and make it responsive.
problemStatement:
Build a complete page layout with a header, sidebar, main content, and footer using CSS Grid Template Areas. **HTML structure:** ```html
Header
Sidebar
Main Content
Footer
``` **CSS requirements (desktop ≥ 768px):** - Use `grid-template-areas` to define a layout: - First row: header spanning two columns. - Second row: sidebar on left, main on right. - Third row: footer spanning two columns. - The grid should have `grid-template-columns: 250px 1fr;` and `grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;`. - The `.page` should have `min-height: 100vh;` so it fills the viewport. - Apply the areas: `.site-header { grid-area: header; }`, `.sidebar { grid-area: sidebar; }`, `.main-content { grid-area: main; }`, `.site-footer { grid-area: footer; }`. - Add a gap of 10px. - Give each area a distinct background colour and some padding. **Mobile (max-width: 767px):** - Change `grid-template-areas` to stack everything in a single column: ```css grid-template-areas: "header" "main" "sidebar" "footer"; grid-template-columns: 1fr; grid-template-rows: auto; /* let content decide */ ``` - (Keep the same gap and styling). Write the full CSS (can be internal stylesheet) including the media query. Use the universal reset.
hints: Area names are case‑sensitive, use lowercase.
In mobile, you can reorder the visual placement by changing the area order, even though HTML order stays the same.
Don't forget to set `min-height: 100vh;` on the container to push footer down when content is short.
expectedOutput: A responsive page layout that switches from two‑column to single‑column on small screens, using template areas.
